A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same theoretical paper, including complete Appendices A and B. The text, rendered equations, and algorithm displays support a reliable comparison without identifiable material gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports convergence theorems and proofs, including in its appendices. The deep-learning outcomes and DenseNet/CIFAR-10 example are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, with proof appendices and no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Empirical examples remain attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. The introductory Padam formula changes from g_t / vhat_t^(-p) to m_t / vhat_t^p, correcting its inconsistency with the existing Algorithm 1 rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts dataset-based training or evaluation. The retained DenseNet/CIFAR-10 example is motivation attributed to Huang et al. (2017).

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparators. The theoretical comparisons involving AMSGrad, corrected RMSProp, SGD, and Chen et al. (2018) remain unchanged; the added citations are related-work discussion.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols appear in either version. Step-size and parameter choices used in the convergence results are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The theoretical discussions of sparse gradients and step-size choices in Remarks 3.6–3.8 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. Expectations in the convergence bounds remain theoretical quantities.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. Theorem 3.3, Corollaries 3.5, 3.9, and 3.11, and their stated convergence-rate comparisons retain the same results.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.2 corrects the gradient inner-product sign from plus to minus in the smoothness definition. Appendix B.1 repairs the induction bounding v_t and vhat_t by G_infty squared, correcting the recursion and explicitly using the maximum update. These are localized mathematical repairs; theorem conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract removes AdaGrad from the algorithms claimed as special cases of Padam. The central convergence guarantees and claimed advantages over existing bounds remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Following Assumption 3.1, v1 says the Euclidean gradient bound is often larger by a factor of sqrt(d). V2 specifies approximately equal gradient coordinates as the relevant condition and supplies the two-sided norm inequality, making this interpretation more precise.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode and parameter prescriptions are retained. Neither version supplies experimental implementation details, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Li and Orabona (2018) and Zou and Shen (2018), briefly discussing their convergence assumptions. The existing research positioning and comparison with Chen et al. (2018) remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and spelling corrections, expands the related-work and norm-comparison paragraphs, and adds an Appendix A lead-in and a parenthetical lemma label. Section order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Local reflow places the notation block entirely on page 5 and shifts the page break within Lemma A.2. Paragraph indentation also changes on page 13. The single-column format and algorithm displays remain; neither version contains figures or results tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency through the corrected smoothness definition, repaired Lemma A.1 proof, and introductory update aligned with Algorithm 1. Removing the AdaGrad special-case claim and qualifying the norm comparison also improve precision. These are useful localized repairs while the central convergence contribution remains stable.
